title: Do MAI-DxO's retrospective results establish benefits for real patients?
summary: Microsoft reported 83% diagnostic accuracy over 304 retrospective complex cases. The reported clinician comparison used a smaller 56-case subset; patient benefits are unproven.
scope: The 304-case evaluation and the 56-case physician subset must not be treated as equal comparison samples.
next: Prospective clinical evaluations with independent review, diagnostic safety and patient outcomes.
events: Microsoft described sequential-diagnosis benchmarks and its diagnostic orchestrator.
The different evaluation denominators and prospective validation limits were documented.
historyPolicy: Future material evidence is append-only. Preserve this version.
